page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-64 is a memory-optimized server instance featuring 64 vCPUs and 512 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with x86_64 architecture, it contains 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled and dedicated CPU allocation. The processor includes 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache configurations. It supports AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, and BMI2 instruction sets, though it lacks AVX-512 capabilities. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the n2d-highmem-64 demonstrates strong multi-core CPU performance, scoring in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and PassMark CPU extended instructions. Memory performance is highly capable, with cached small-block read bandwidth reaching 4074.82 GB/sec and large-block write bandwidth at 113.39 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. However, uncached large-block read bandwidth is average at 176.05 GB/sec. Database operations are a notable strength, with PassMark database operations scoring in the top 25% and Redis SET operations achieving 63.0 million operations per second. Single-core performance and text processing tasks generally fall into the average tier.

From a resource density perspective, the n2d-highmem-64 offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The lack of local storage means all storage operations must rely on network-attached volumes, which is a key architectural tradeoff. Given its high memory capacity and strong multi-core and database benchmark results, this server is best suited for large-scale database deployments, in-memory caching layers like Redis, memory-intensive data processing, and enterprise applications requiring substantial memory overhead per vCPU.
